knowledge:
- key_parameters: fCol=Column name specifying the fraction in cleanData() (defaults to "Search ID") ;; rank=Filtering rank in toFilter() (e.g., rank = 1) ;; purpose=Format of the output table in getNormTable() ("analysis" for downstream steps or "export" for human-readable tables) ;; scenar=Scenario to use for clustering in clusterComp() ("A" or "B") ;; PearsCor=Pearson correlation distance measure in clusterComp() ("centered" or "uncentered") ;; sample=Sample type in assignClusters() ("labeled" or "unlabeled") ;; method=Linkage method in assignClusters() ('single', 'average', or 'complete') ;; cutoff=Height cutoff for cluster assignment in assignClusters()
- alternatives: The package offers two entry points: a full peptide-to-protein workflow starting from raw peptide tables, and a protein-only workflow starting from pre-normalized protein tables (preferred if custom protein estimation or normalization methods are desired).
- when_to_use: Use when analyzing SILAC-labeled complexome profiling data (e.g., from BN-PAGE or density gradient centrifugation) to compare protein co-migration and abundance between two biological samples (labeled vs. unlabeled).
- pitfalls: Do not use Scenario A for quantitative comparison of proteins between SILAC label states (use Scenario B instead), as Scenario A normalizes each label state independently. Ensure the input file contains specific columns with exact names and formats (e.g., "PSM Ambiguity", "Precursor Area", "Protein Descriptions" containing "GN=" for gene names, and "Search ID" representing fractions alphabetically).

workflows.name: peptide_to_protein_workflow
workflows.intent: Perform a full analysis starting from raw peptide-level tables to clean, filter, select representative peptides, normalize, cluster, and visualize SILAC complexome profiling data.
input: peptide_input.txt (tab-delimited peptide table containing columns like "PSM Ambiguity", "Precursor Area", "Search ID", etc.)
workflows.stages: 1. Import peptide data ;; 2. Clean and filter data ;; 3. Split modifications and simplify protein rows ;; 4. Select representative peptides ;; 5. Generate normalized protein tables ;; 6. Perform hierarchical clustering ;; 7. Assign clusters and export results ;; 8. Visualize peptide and cluster summaries
workflows.code:
library (ComPrAn)
inputFile <- system.file ( "extData" , "data.txt" , package = "ComPrAn" )
peptides <- peptideImport (inputFile)
peptides <- cleanData (peptides, fCol = "Search ID" )
peptides <- toFilter (peptides, rank = 1 )
peptides <- splitModLab (peptides)
peptides <- simplifyProteins (peptides)
peptide_index <- pickPeptide (peptides)
protein <- "P52815"
max_frac <- 23
allPeptidesPlot (peptide_index,protein, max_frac = max_frac)
listOnlyOneLabState <- onlyInOneLabelState (peptide_index)
forAnalysis <- getNormTable (peptide_index, purpose = "analysis" )
forExport <- getNormTable (peptide_index, purpose = "export" )
clusteringDF <- clusterComp (forAnalysis, scenar = "A" , PearsCor = "centered" )
labTab_clust <- assignClusters ( .listDf = clusteringDF, sample = "labeled" , method = 'average' , cutoff = 0.85 )
unlabTab_clust <- assignClusters ( .listDf = clusteringDF, sample = "unlabeled" , method = 'average' , cutoff = 0.85 )
makeBarPlotClusterSummary (labTab_clust, name = 'labeled' )
makeBarPlotClusterSummary (unlabTab_clust, name = 'unlabeled' )
tableForClusterExport <- exportClusterAssignments (labTab_clust,unlabTab_clust)

workflows.name: protein_only_workflow
workflows.intent: Analyze SILAC complexome profiling data starting directly from pre-normalized protein intensity tables to perform clustering and visualization.
input: normalized_proteins.txt (tab-delimited normalized protein table with columns "Protein Group Accessions", "Protein Descriptions", "scenario", "label", and fraction columns "1" to "n")
exampleGroup.txt (tab-delimited table containing a list of proteins belonging to a specific group)
workflows.stages: 1. Import normalized protein data ;; 2. Visualize individual protein profiles ;; 3. Visualize group profiles and co-migration ;; 4. Perform hierarchical clustering ;; 5. Assign clusters and export results ;; 6. Visualize cluster summaries
workflows.code:
library (ComPrAn)
inputFile <- system.file ( "extData" , "dataNormProts.txt" , package = "ComPrAn" )
forAnalysis <- protImportForAnalysis (inputFile)
protein <- "P52815"
max_frac <- 23
proteinPlot (forAnalysis[forAnalysis $ scenario == "B" ,], protein, max_frac)
groupDataFileName <- system.file ( "extData" , "exampleGroup.txt" , package= "ComPrAn" )
groupName <- 'group1'
groupData <- data.table :: fread (groupDataFileName)
groupHeatMap ( dataFrame = forAnalysis[forAnalysis $ scenario == "B" ,], groupData, groupName)
groupDataVector <- c ( "Q16540" , "P52815" , "P09001" , "Q13405" , "Q9H2W6" )
groupName <- 'group1'
max_frac <- 23
oneGroupTwoLabelsCoMigration (forAnalysis, max_frac = max_frac, groupDataVector,groupName)
group1DataVector <- c ( "Q16540" , "P52815" , "P09001" , "Q13405" , "Q9H2W6" )
group1Name <- 'group1'
group2DataVector <- c ( "Q9NVS2" , "Q9NWU5" , "Q9NX20" , "Q9NYK5" , "Q9NZE8" )
group2Name <- 'group2'
max_frac <- 23
twoGroupsWithinLabelCoMigration ( dataFrame = forAnalysis, max_frac = max_frac, group1Data = group1DataVector, group1Name = group1Name, group2Data = group2DataVector, group2Name = group2Name)
clusteringDF <- clusterComp (forAnalysis, scenar = "A" , PearsCor = "centered" )
labTab_clust <- assignClusters ( .listDf = clusteringDF, sample = "labeled" , method = 'average' , cutoff = 0.85 )
unlabTab_clust <- assignClusters ( .listDf = clusteringDF, sample = "unlabeled" , method = 'average' , cutoff = 0.85 )
makeBarPlotClusterSummary (labTab_clust, name = 'labeled' )
makeBarPlotClusterSummary (unlabTab_clust, name = 'unlabeled' )
tableForClusterExport <- exportClusterAssignments (labTab_clust,unlabTab_clust)
